Currently
column2: different formulas are used to estimate the space that may be

column1: taken by WQEs in the SQ during a single packet transmit. This space is
called stop room
column2: and it's checked in the end of packet transmit to find

column1: out if the next packet could overflow the SQ. If it could
tells the kernel to stop sending next packets.
Many factors affect the stop room:
1. Padding with NOPs to avoid WQEs spanning over page boundaries.
2. Enabled and disabled offloads (TLS
3. The maximum size of a WQE.
The padding is performed before every WQE if it doesn't fit the current
page.
The current formula assumes that only one padding will be required per
packet
column2: and it doesn't take into account that the WQEs posted during the

column1: transmission of a single packet might exceed the page size in very rare
circumstances. For example
column2: to hit this condition with 4096-byte pages

column1: TLS offload will have to interrupt an almost-full MPWQE session
the resync flow and try to transmit a near to maximum amount of data.
To avoid SQ overflows in such rare cases after MPWQE is added
patch introduces a more robust formula to estimate the stop room. The
new formula uses the fact that a WQE of size X will not require more
than X-1 WQEBBs of padding. More exact estimations are possible
they result in much more complex and error-prone code for little gain.
Before this patch
column2: the TLS stop room included space for both INNOVA and

column1: ConnectX TLS offloads that couldn't run at the same time anyway
patch accounts only for the active one.
